scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9106: A user on pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reports they lost all
connectivity -- pc_0_0 can't reach pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) or anything across the
fabric. The team is convinced it is the host -- they say "pc_0_0's host NIC or
its cabling is faulty" and want the workstation's network card and cable swapped.
Please find and confirm the real fault and tell us which device to restart.

injection.action: take down pc_0_0's access link (eth2) on leaf_router_0_0

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth2 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
The real fault is on leaf_router_0_0: pc_0_0's access link -- the host-facing
interface eth2 (leaf_router_0_0 -> pc_0_0) -- is DOWN, so pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) is
cut off at its own top-of-rack leaf and cannot reach pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) or anything
beyond. The ticket MISDESCRIBES the fault as a host-side problem, but pc_0_0
itself is fine: the down interface is the LEAF's access port (leaf_router_0_0
eth2), not the host's NIC or cable. Swapping pc_0_0's network card / cabling would
not bring the leaf's administratively/operationally down access port back up.

The correct diagnosis identifies leaf_router_0_0 (host-facing access link eth2
down) as the faulty device and explicitly REJECTS the host-NIC/cable cause: the
fault is on the leaf's access port, so the host hardware is not at fault. An agent
that blames pc_0_0's NIC / cable has followed the ticket's misdescription instead
of the evidence.
scenario.fix_spec:
Bring pc_0_0's access link back up: on leaf_router_0_0, `ip link set eth2 up`.
Once eth2 is UP again, pc_0_0 reattaches to its leaf and reaches pc_0_1 across
the fabric. pc_0_0's host NIC / cabling needs no change.
scoring_axes: must-identify-link-down: identifies pc_0_0's access link (leaf_router_0_0 eth2) is down, not a host NIC/cable fault
bonus-rules-out-host-nic: notes the down interface is leaf_router_0_0's access port (eth2), not pc_0_0's hardware, rejecting the "bad host NIC/cable" cause

results.actual:

--- 10.0.1.2 ping statistics ---
2 packets transmitted, 0 received, 100% packet loss, time 1020ms

agent.diagnosis_text:
The failure is on the fabric side, not the host. The affected component is the host-facing access interface eth2 on leaf_router_0_0. That interface is administratively down, so the leaf never sees pc_0_0’s frames and cannot answer ARP for the default gateway.

Mechanism: With the leaf’s eth2 down, L2 adjacency to pc_0_0 is lost. From pc_0_0 we see 10.0.0.1 (its default gateway) is unreachable and the ARP entry remains INCOMPLETE, so all traffic to anywhere off-host fails at the first hop. This exactly matches the user’s “lost all connectivity”.

Localization evidence:
- pc_0_0: default via 10.0.0.1; ping 10.0.0.1 = 100% loss; “ip neigh” shows 10.0.0.1 INCOMPLETE.
- leaf_router_0_0: eth2 is DOWN (ip -br link), not RUNNING in ifconfig, and ethtool reports “Link detected: no” on eth2 despite having 10.0.0.1/24 configured. Core links (eth0/eth1) are UP and BGP routes are present (e.g., route to 10.0.1.0/24 via 172.16.0.8), proving the fabric itself is healthy. The peer leaf and pc_0_1 segment are normal (pc_0_1 can reach 10.0.1.1).

Root cause: leaf_router_0_0’s access interface eth2 toward pc_0_0 was administratively disabled.

Corrective fix: Re-enable the port on the leaf. Recommended action: restart networking on leaf_router_0_0 (or simply bring up eth2). After eth2 is up, pc_0_0 should ARP 10.0.0.1 successfully and regain full fabric connectivity. No host NIC or cabling replacement is needed.

Recommends re-enabling eth2 on leaf_router_0_0 (or restarting networking) which matches the expected fix of bringing the access link back up so the host regains connectivity.

The log contains concrete observations showing pc_0_0 cannot ARP its gateway and leaf_router_0_0 eth2 is DOWN while other fabric links are UP; the agent correctly attributes the outage to the leaf access port being down and rejects a host-NIC/cable blame. The only weak point is asserting the interface is specifically ‘administratively’ down — the logs show it is down but do not explicitly prove admin vs. physical/operator-down.
